post/xconda-production-map.title: From one scenario to a finished video: the XCONDA production map in 7 steps
post/xconda-production-map.summary: Cubeberry's AI video starts with a scenario, is produced in XCONDA, gets its sound in Suno and is finished in Premiere Pro. This post lays the whole order out as a single map, with the input, deliverable and checks for each step; the detailed how-tos continue in the series.

blocks.text: Cubeberry's AI video starts with a scenario, is produced in XCONDA, gets its sound in Suno, and is finished in Premiere Pro. This post lays out the whole order as a single map, with the input, deliverable and checks for each step; the detailed how-tos follow in the series.
AI video production EP.00 — the full map. Start here if this is your first time.

Hello, this is XCONDA. Cubeberry's AI video starts with a scenario, is produced in XCONDA, gets its sound in Suno, and is finished in Premiere Pro. This post shows the whole sequence as one map, with an explanation for each step. The detailed method for every step continues in the series below.

Key summary: the process is 7 steps — preparation (01–04), video (05) and post (06–07). This post shows that order as a single map and sets out, for each step, what goes in, what comes out and what to check before moving on.
Who this is for: people making AI video for the first time, people who have used the tools but struggle to make cuts connect, and teams that need to share one production order.
How to read: if you are new, start here; when you get stuck on a step, jump to the detailed post for that step. The series keeps going, so this post doubles as a table of contents.
The flow at a glance
Scenario → references → text storyboard → storyboard and blocking → video generation → sound → edit and finish

The area outlined in yellow on the map is 04 storyboard and blocking, because it is the link between preparation and video work. The outputs of the earlier steps gather there, and the key images confirmed there become the basis for the prompts in 05. If you dislike the result at 05, you fix the problem area and generate again — that is where the flow turns into a loop.
Why four preparation steps before generating video?

Give a video AI nothing but text and you get a different face, different clothes and a different composition every time. Stitch the cuts together and it looks like a different actor performed each one. The preparation steps exist to lock that wobble down before any video is made.

The easiest analogy is our CEO's time directing dramas at KBS. On set you confirm the actors, build the set and check the order and framing of cuts on a storyboard before rolling the camera — because fixing things on paper costs almost nothing, while fixing them after the shoot means shooting again. AI video also spends credits every time you roll. Checking a badly framed video and starting over is the same as reshooting the entire scene.
The key here is the division of labour between text and images. Each does what the other cannot.

However precisely you describe a face or an outfit in words, it never conveys what an image does, and conversely the order and timing of cuts are hard to convey with images. So characters and spaces are handled by images, and flow and movement by text.
Why cuts jump is covered in the post on background and cut consistency, and practical fixes in the guide to the 9-cut curse.
Step by step
Each step is laid out as input → deliverable → check before moving on. The check is what you verify yourself before going on to the next step.
01. Write the scenario

items: Input: idea, proposal
Deliverable: a locked scenario
Check before moving on: are the characters and locations decided?

blocks.text: Everything starts here. Without characters and locations you cannot build the references for the next step. Rather than naming an emotion ("sad"), write it as something visible — "hides the broken shard behind her back" — so it is easier to break into cuts later.
02. Get the reference images

items: Tools: Claude, the XCONDA FLEXBOARD skill, GPT Image, XCONDA Turn
Input: the scenario
Deliverable: a face image per character (character sheet), location images (background sheets), and cut images made in Turn where needed
Check before moving on: does every character have a face image, do you have the location images, and did you build the hard-to-shoot cuts in Turn?

blocks.text: If you already have references, use them as they are alongside the scenario. If not, the FLEXBOARD skill reads the scenario and writes the prompts that make a character sheet and a background sheet. Copy those prompts into GPT Image to make the images, then feed the images back in.

Using XCONDA Turn: two things from a 360° virtual set. Turn builds a virtual set you can look around 360° from a single photo or a text description. Because you build one space first and then turn the camera inside it to pick angles, doors, windows and props stay in place as the cuts change. Method A — build a background sheet: 1) put one face of the background sheet (the front image) into Turn. 2) Build the left, right and back sides from it. 3) Use the four sides together as the background reference; this feeds the background reference for 05 video generation. Method B — build storyboard cut images: 1) create the 360° virtual set. 2) Place characters and props inside it. 3) Turn to the angle you want and pull the cut image; this goes straight into the 04 storyboard as a cut image.

Why do it this way? Generate the background separately for each cut and the windows, furniture and props move from cut to cut. On a real set you build the set once and only move the camera inside it — the same idea: fix the space first, then change the angle. Method B is especially useful when you want to place a complex composition yourself, because text alone rarely produces it.
Common mistake: putting several face images of the same person in at once blends and smears the face. The rule is one face image per character.
03. Text storyboard and FLEXBOARD prompts

items: Tools: Claude, the XCONDA FLEXBOARD skill
Input: the scenario and the reference images from 02
Deliverable: a text storyboard (length, camera, action, dialogue and sound effects per cut) and the prompts for FLEXBOARD
Check before moving on: does every cut state a start action and an end action?

blocks.text: A text storyboard is the scene written out in words first. At this stage you also check that the cut lengths add up, that no single cut is crammed with action, that cuts do not jump awkwardly, and that the number of characters is right. Where to download and install the skills is covered lower down.
04. Storyboard and blocking video

items: Tools: XCONDA FLEXBOARD, XCONDA Blocking Board
Input: the FLEXBOARD prompts from 03, and the cut images made in Turn at 02 (the hard-to-shoot cuts)
Deliverable: a key image per cut (storyboard images) and a blocking puppet video
Check before moving on: is each cut's key frame the composition you intended, and does the puppet video's movement match your intent?

blocks.text: FLEXBOARD is a storyboard tool that splits the scenario into cuts, generates an image for each cut and lays them out on one screen. It holds up to 36 cuts on a screen, and you can leave the good cuts alone and fix only the ones with problems. The click-by-click walkthrough is written up in the FLEXBOARD guide.

XCONDA Blocking Board: showing character movement as video. Movement like "enters through the left door, walks around the table and stops at the window" invites the model to walk the wrong way when it is only written down, and scenes with several characters moving at once drift easily. Blocking Board produces a video of grey mannequins (puppets) moving inside the space; add that video to video generation and Seedance reads the movement from video rather than text. The division of labour: reference images handle faces and costumes, the puppet video handles paths and timing.

Blocking Board is currently open as a free beta (up to the stage before video generation). Paste a scene prompt and press Create to compose the 3D space and characters, add cameras with Add camera, and send to Seedance from the Output tab. See the Blocking Board beta notice for the full introduction.
The puppet does not need to look human. Position, direction and speed are enough. Just remember to attach the puppet video at 05 video generation.
Fixing here is the cheapest. Generate video with the wrong composition and you regenerate several times at the video stage. Fix it in the storyboard first.
05. Seedance prompts and video generation

items: Tools: Claude, the Seedance prompt skill, the prompt editor, XCONDA
Input: the FLEXBOARD prompts and text storyboard, reference images, the storyboard, the blocking puppet video from 04, and audio references if needed
Deliverable: a two-column prompt editor with Korean and English side by side, and the video generated in XCONDA
How to revise: tell the editor in conversation what to fix, it updates the prompt, and you generate again. Repeat the loop until you are happy.

blocks.text: The Seedance prompt skill builds prompts for Seedance 2.5 from the key images. It organises them with a four-director system and a ten-block structure, and lets you revise with Korean and English side by side. Revise in Korean and the English is rewritten to match, so you never have to edit the English separately. The skill is being prepared for download from the XCONDA hub.

What goes into the XCONDA video generation screen: all four are required. ① Reference images (character sheets, background sheets, Turn sheets, props): they fix faces, costumes and spaces. ② The storyboard (the per-cut images made at 04): it fixes composition, movement and cut order. ③ The Seedance prompt (finished in the editor): it directs movement, timing and camera. ④ The blocking puppet video (made in Blocking Board at 04): it fixes the character's path and travel route.

If any one of the four is missing, the AI fills that part in as it likes. Drop the reference images, for example, and even if the prompt says "the woman in @image1" it cannot tell who that is, so the face changes from cut to cut. Drop the storyboard and the composition changes every time even with the same prompt; drop the puppet video and characters walk in a different direction from the prompt, or several characters' paths cross each other.

On the generation screen, choose Reference (Ref-to-video) mode and type @ in the prompt to say which reference is which. Aspect ratio, resolution, length and High Quality are set on the Options tab, and Seedance 2.5 can produce up to 30 seconds at a time.

While you iterate on revisions and regenerations, the recently added Draft feature helps: check the result at 480p first and turn only the drafts you like into 1080p finals. Note that the final is generated fresh from the same assets as the draft, so fine details can differ slightly, and drafts are valid for 7 days after generation. See the Draft notice for details.
06. Sound

items: Tools: Suno
Input: the mood and length of the video finished at 05
Deliverable: sound files for the video
Check before moving on: does it match the video's length and mood?

blocks.text: Sound is made after the video is finished, using the video's mood and length as the brief. The detailed method for this step continues in the series.
07. Combine video and sound

items: Tools: Premiere Pro
Input: the clips generated at 05 and the sound made at 06
Deliverable: the finished video
Check before moving on: cut connections, levels and subtitles

blocks.text: The last step. Before joining the cuts, keep the references from 02 and the text storyboard from 03 beside you and run through once more to confirm that costumes, props and backgrounds do not change from cut to cut.
One-page summary per step
So you can check as you read the map, the input, deliverable and pre-handover checks are gathered in one table.
Five common mistakes

items: Generating video first: check with images and you only redo the one wrong cut. With video you redo the whole thing.
Adding several face images of the same character: the faces blend. One per character is the rule.
Putting only some of the four inputs into generation: whatever is missing — references, storyboard, prompt or puppet video — the AI fills in as it likes.
Expecting faces and expressions from the puppet video: puppets carry position, direction and speed only. Faces belong to the reference images.
Regenerating cuts that already look good: fix only the cuts with problems.

AI video production continues one step per post. Posts already published are linked, and the rest will be released in order.
Good companions: the post on why to storyboard before generating video, and the production case study that locks cut consistency with Turn and FLEXBOARD.

qna/access-edit-delete-data.title: How do I view, correct or delete my data?
qna/access-edit-delete-data.summary: Email cubeberry@cuberry.kr, call +82-70-8095-2302 (weekdays 10:00–17:00 KST), or make the request in your XCONDA account settings. After verifying your identity we forward the request to the relevant company and answer within 45 days, at no charge. Requests through an authorised representative are also accepted. The data protection officer is the CEO, Jinseo Lee.

qna/ai-video-training-courses.title: Do you run AI video production courses or webinars?
qna/ai-video-training-courses.summary: Yes. We are planning regular webinars, with the first session in October and one session each month after that. Dates and how to sign up are announced in the hub notices.

qna/before-chargeback.title: What should I do before filing a chargeback?
qna/before-chargeback.summary: Contact cubeberry@cuberry.kr before filing a chargeback — support often resolves the issue faster. Stripe disputes are handled by the US entity and PortOne disputes by the Korean entity. A chargeback found to be unjustified may lead to the account being suspended or terminated under our terms.

qna/best-stage-to-edit.title: At which stage is editing most efficient?
qna/best-stage-to-edit.summary: At the storyboard stage. Once video is generated with the wrong framing you end up regenerating at the video stage several times. Fix framing, characters and props on the per-shot images in FLEXBOARD first, then move to video, and you regenerate far less.

qna/blocking-board-export.title: What can I export from Blocking Board?
qna/blocking-board-export.summary: For a reviewed scene you can export the English prompt (for Seedance), a shot list, floor-plan and frame PNGs, and a shot-book PDF. Playing the scene also exports a previs clip as WebM.

qna/cancel-subscription.title: How do I cancel my subscription?
qna/cancel-subscription.summary: You can cancel yourself at any time in Account Settings — no need to contact support. Cancelling stops automatic billing from the next renewal date. Charges already paid are not refunded pro rata, but you can request a refund within 7 days if the credits are unused, subject to our refund policy. After cancelling, remaining subscription credits stay usable for up to one year from the date they were granted.

qna/card-information-security.title: Is my card information stored safely?
qna/card-information-security.summary: Card details are handled by Stripe or by PortOne (Toss Payments, KakaoPay, Eximbay). Cubeberry's servers never store a full card number — only the last four digits and the expiry date, for verification.

qna/commercial-use.title: Can I use XCONDA output commercially?
qna/commercial-use.summary: Under our terms, you own what you create with XCONDA, and no clause restricts commercial use. Uploading or creating content that infringes someone else's intellectual property is prohibited, so please confirm that you hold the rights to the images and footage you use.

qna/commission-video-production.title: Can Cubeberry produce a video for me?
qna/commission-video-production.summary: Yes. Cubeberry handles planning, story, AI generation, editing and post-production in one team, built on XCONDA. We have produced web dramas, animation, documentaries, advertising and corporate films. Contact us to discuss a project.

qna/company-business-info.title: Which company operates XCONDA?
qna/company-business-info.summary: XCONDA is developed and operated by Cubeberry Co., Ltd. (주식회사 큐브베리). CEO: Jinseo Lee (이진서). Business registration number 480-88-03079; e-commerce registration 2026-광주동구-0289. Address: 2F, 69-12 Chungjang-ro, Dong-gu, Jeonnam-Gwangju 61482, Republic of Korea. Phone +82-70-8095-2302, email cubeberry@cuberry.kr, weekdays 10:00–17:00 KST. Servers run on Amazon Web Services. The registration can be verified on the Korean Fair Trade Commission site (https://www.ftc.go.kr/bizCommPop.do?wrkr_no=4808803079).

qna/contact-inquiry.title: How do I contact support?
qna/contact-inquiry.summary: Support is handled in one place for every customer. Email cubeberry@cuberry.kr or call +82-70-8095-2302, weekdays 10:00–17:00 KST (lunch 12:00–13:00). The US entity (Cubeberry Co., Ltd, Delaware) can be reached at info@cubeberry.ai or +1-888-202-1989; its New York address is 276 5th Ave, Ste 704-2816, New York, NY 10001. Refunds for purchases made through the US entity go through the same support desk.

qna/cookies.title: Do you use cookies?
qna/cookies.summary: Yes. We use strictly necessary cookies for sign-in and security, analytics cookies for usage statistics and error tracking, and preference cookies that remember settings such as language. You can block or delete cookies in your browser, though some features may then be limited. For users in Europe and the UK, non-essential cookies are used only with consent, and consent can be withdrawn at any time.

qna/credit-expiry-and-refund-policy.title: What are the credit validity and refund rules?
qna/credit-expiry-and-refund-policy.summary: Subscription credits are valid for up to one year from the date they are granted, and credit packs for one year from purchase; unused credits then lapse automatically. A full refund can be requested within 7 days of payment if none of the credits from that purchase have been used. After 7 days, or if any credit has been used, no refund is available. On refund, only the credits from that purchase are reclaimed; credits rolled over from earlier are kept. Nothing in the terms limits statutory refund or withdrawal rights in your country of residence. See the refund section below for the process.

qna/credit-packs-and-price.title: What are credit packs and how much do they cost?
qna/credit-packs-and-price.summary: A credit pack is a one-time purchase that gives you a fixed number of credits. It does not renew automatically. In Korea (KRW, VAT included): Starter Pack V1 ₩10,450 (2,020 credits), Starter Pack V2 ₩31,350 (6,200), Pro Pack V1 ₩52,250 (10,500), Pro Pack V2 ₩99,000 (21,500), Master Pack ₩495,000 (114,000). Outside Korea (USD, tax excluded): $6.90, $20.90, $34.90, $67.90 and $369.90. Credits are valid for one year from purchase.

qna/credit-transfer-cash-withdrawal.title: Can I transfer credits or cash them out? What happens to credits if I leave?
qna/credit-transfer-cash-withdrawal.summary: No. Credits have no cash value and cannot be transferred or sold. If you close your account or it is terminated, remaining credits lapse. Purchases that qualify for a refund are refunded first.

qna/current-discount-events.title: Are there any discounts running now?
qna/current-discount-events.summary: We are running a Seedance 2.5 promotion to mark the FLEXBOARD launch. In Korea, 30% usage discount plus 10% price discount adds up to 40%; in the US, up to 30% usage discount. It runs from 11:00 on 7 October 2026 to 11:00 on 6 November 2026 (KST).

qna/data-operation-location.title: Where is XCONDA data processed and stored?
qna/data-operation-location.summary: XCONDA runs on Amazon Web Services, and stored data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Personal data may be processed and stored in Korea, our primary location, and in the United States (our US entity, Stripe and cloud providers) and other countries where our service providers operate. Cross-border transfers rely on standard contractual clauses and data processing agreements.

qna/error-support.title: What should I do if something goes wrong?
qna/error-support.summary: Credits charged for a failed generation or a service outage are refunded automatically. For any other error, email cubeberry@cuberry.kr (phone +82-70-8095-2302, weekdays 10:00–17:00 KST). Include your account email, a screenshot of the error and the time it happened so we can look into it quickly.

qna/eu-uk-withdrawal-refund.title: Can I withdraw or get a refund in Europe or the UK?
qna/eu-uk-withdrawal-refund.summary: Consumers in the EEA and the UK have a 14-day right of withdrawal for digital services. Before payment you confirm that you agree to immediate delivery of the service and credits, and that the withdrawal right ends when you use credits from that purchase. If you have not used any credits, you can withdraw within 14 days of payment and receive a full refund.

qna/flexboard-auto-refine-instant-apply.title: When should I use Auto Refine and Instant Apply?
qna/flexboard-auto-refine-instant-apply.summary: Auto Refine refines an idea or a rough scenario and breaks it into shots. Instant Apply applies a scenario you have already organised, quickly and as written. If you prepared a written board with the FLEXBOARD skill first, Instant Apply is the easier path.

qna/flexboard-character-consistency.title: How do I keep the same character across shots?
qna/flexboard-character-consistency.summary: Register a character (Cast) card and a background card under Reference Assets in Scene Settings. Each card carries a token such as @image1 or @image2, and including that token in a shot description shows which character and background were used. Register one card per character.

qna/flexboard-cut-count-and-length.title: How many shots can FLEXBOARD hold, and how long can each be?
qna/flexboard-cut-count-and-length.summary: Up to 36 shots per board. Set the count in Number of Panels and each shot's length in Shot Length, between 4 and 30 seconds. For example, 9 shots at 15 seconds add up to roughly 2 minutes 15 seconds.

qna/flexboard-download-storyboard.title: Can I download the storyboard I made in FLEXBOARD?
qna/flexboard-download-storyboard.summary: Yes. From the top right of the Edit Panel, choose Download CUT ZIP in Panel view to get all shot images at once, or Download Sheet in Sheet view to get a single sheet. It is the easiest way to share a board with a team or a client.

qna/flexboard-edit-single-cut.title: Can I fix just one shot I don't like?
qna/flexboard-edit-single-cut.summary: Yes. In Edit Panel's Panel view, press Edit on the shot you want to change and only that shot is revised. For a simple change, write one sentence in Quick Edit (for example, "change only the glasses, keep the pose and background"). To change the camera, pick Shot Size, Camera Angle and Camera Movement in Detailed Edit and regenerate. Every other shot stays as it is.

qna/flexboard-panel-vs-sheet.title: What is the difference between Panel and Sheet view?
qna/flexboard-panel-vs-sheet.summary: Panel view shows one card per shot with its image, scene description, dialogue, sound cues and an Edit button — use it to read and fix individual shots. Sheet view shows the shot images large, without descriptions — use it to judge whether the sequence flows. The recommended order is Sheet first for flow, then Panel shot by shot.

qna/governing-law-disputes.title: Which law applies if there is a dispute?
qna/governing-law-disputes.summary: If you contracted with the Korean entity (Cubeberry Co., Ltd.), Korean law applies and unresolved disputes go to the Korean courts. If you contracted with the US entity (Cubeberry Co., Ltd, Delaware), New York law applies and disputes go to the state or federal courts in New York County. Mandatory consumer protections in your country of residence still apply.

qna/how-credits-are-deducted.title: How are credits deducted?
qna/how-credits-are-deducted.summary: Credits are charged differently depending on the feature and model used. The credit cost per generation is shown on the generate button or the selection screen, so check before generating. In Turn, for example, the cost per generation is shown for each image model, and FLEXBOARD's image regenerate button shows the credits it needs. Credits lost to a service outage or a failed generation are restored automatically. When you hold several batches of credits, the ones expiring earliest are used first.

qna/how-to-access-hub.title: How do I get to the hub?
qna/how-to-access-hub.summary: On the XCONDA website (xconda.ai), open the Resources menu and choose Hub.

qna/how-to-install-skills.title: How do I install a skill?
qna/how-to-install-skills.summary: Per the Claude help centre: 1) download the skill ZIP from the hub (one ZIP per skill); 2) in Claude go to Customize > Skills; 3) press '+' and choose Create skill; 4) choose Upload a skill and upload the ZIP; 5) when it appears in the list, switch it on. Code execution must be enabled under Capabilities in settings.

qna/how-to-request-refund.title: How do I request a refund, and how long does it take?
qna/how-to-request-refund.summary: Contact support (cubeberry@cuberry.kr or +82-70-8095-2302, weekdays 10:00–17:00 KST) with your account email, order number, payment date and reason. Requests are reviewed within 2–3 business days, and once approved the charge is reversed to the original payment method; the amount can take 7–14 business days to appear. The same rule applies to a first subscription payment, a renewal, an upgrade and credit packs: a full refund within 7 days if none of the credits from that purchase have been used. Refunds are processed by the company you bought from — the US entity for Stripe payments, the Korean entity for PortOne payments.

qna/how-to-sign-up.title: How do I sign up?
qna/how-to-sign-up.summary: Create an account on the XCONDA website (xconda.ai). You can sign in with Google, Facebook or X, or use an email address and password. You must be 18 or older, provide accurate details and keep your credentials secure. Do not share an account with anyone else. Signing up does not currently include free credits.

qna/hub-languages.title: Can I read the hub in other languages?
qna/hub-languages.summary: Yes. The language buttons at the top of the hub switch between Korean, English, Japanese and Chinese. Each language also has its own address — Korean at the root, and English, Japanese and Chinese under /en/, /ja/ and /zh/ — so you can share a link that opens in the language you want.

qna/international-payment.title: Can I pay from outside Korea?
qna/international-payment.summary: Yes, through two payment paths. With Stripe, the seller is the US entity Cubeberry Co., Ltd (Delaware) and billing is in US dollars, with tax added at checkout depending on where you live. With Toss Payments, KakaoPay or Eximbay (via PortOne), the seller is the Korean entity Cubeberry Co., Ltd and Korean billing is in won. The seller's name appears on the payment screen and the receipt.

qna/is-tax-included.title: Is tax included in the price?
qna/is-tax-included.summary: Korean prices include 10% VAT. Prices outside Korea exclude tax, and sales tax, VAT or GST may be added at checkout depending on where you live. The final amount including tax is shown before you confirm the payment.

qna/minors-eligibility.title: Can minors use XCONDA?
qna/minors-eligibility.summary: No. XCONDA is available only to people aged 18 or older. We do not collect personal data from anyone under 18, and if we learn that we have, we delete it immediately.

qna/mixing-with-live-footage.title: Can I mix live-action footage with AI video?
qna/mixing-with-live-footage.summary: In Reference mode you can add up to 10 videos as references, so footage you shot yourself can be used as reference material. How strongly a referenced video shapes the output depends on the prompt and the footage, so test with a short clip first.

qna/multiple-face-photos-accuracy.title: Does adding more face photos of the same person improve accuracy?
qna/multiple-face-photos-accuracy.summary: Often the opposite. Adding several photos of the same face can blend the features and blur the result. The rule is one face image per character.

qna/non-refundable-cases.title: When is a refund not available?
qna/non-refundable-cases.summary: No refund is available after 7 days from payment, if any credit from that purchase has been used, or if the account was terminated for breaching the terms. These conditions are shown and agreed before payment. Credits lost to a service outage or a failed generation are restored automatically rather than refunded.

qna/output-copyright.title: Who owns the copyright in what I create?
qna/output-copyright.summary: Under our terms you own the content you generate with the service. The XCONDA platform itself (software, technology, trademarks) belongs to Cubeberry Co., Ltd. You grant Cubeberry (the Korean and US entities) a non-exclusive licence to use your content only to provide and improve the service. You may not upload or create content that infringes the intellectual property of others.

qna/payment-failed.title: What should I do if a payment fails?
qna/payment-failed.summary: Common causes are insufficient balance or limit, an expired card, overseas payments blocked, a wrong billing address or CVV, and the card issuer's fraud prevention. Ask your card issuer whether overseas payments are allowed, then check balance, expiry and billing details. If it still fails, try another payment method or email cubeberry@cuberry.kr. For a payment page that will not open, or for declined authorisations, support will check with the payment provider (Stripe, PortOne and others).

qna/payment-seller-name.title: Whose name appears as the seller when I pay?
qna/payment-seller-name.summary: The company you bought from appears on the payment screen and receipt. Payments through Stripe show Cubeberry Co., Ltd (Delaware); payments through Toss Payments, KakaoPay or Eximbay (PortOne) show Cubeberry Co., Ltd (Korea). Refunds are returned to the original payment method by the company you purchased from.

qna/personal-data-collected.title: What personal data do you collect?
qna/personal-data-collected.summary: We collect identifiers such as email, name, account name, IP address and device information; subscription and credit purchase and usage history; payment details such as card brand, last four digits, expiry date and billing address; platform usage logs and cookies; approximate location derived from IP (country and region); and the content you create and the files you upload. We do not collect precise location, health, racial, religious or sexual-orientation data, national ID numbers or passport numbers.

qna/personal-data-retention.title: How long do you keep personal data?
qna/personal-data-retention.summary: Account data is kept for up to 90 days after the account is deleted; payment records for 7 years as required by tax and accounting law; usage data for 2 years; support records for 3 years; and marketing consent records for 30 days after consent is withdrawn. When a retention period ends we delete or anonymise the data. Google Firebase authentication data used for sign-in is removed from servers and backups within 180 days of a deletion request.

qna/personal-data-sale-ads.title: Do you sell my data or use it for advertising?
qna/personal-data-sale-ads.summary: No. We do not sell personal data to third parties and do not share it for targeted advertising. Sensitive personal data is not used for anything beyond delivering the service you requested, security and legal obligations.

qna/prohibited-actions.title: What is prohibited on XCONDA?
qna/prohibited-actions.summary: Using the service for unlawful purposes; uploading or creating content that infringes someone else's intellectual property; reverse engineering, decompiling or hacking the service; creating harmful, offensive or otherwise inappropriate content; sharing account credentials; and accessing the service by automated means without written permission. Violations can lead to restricted access or account termination.

qna/real-person-celebrity-reference.title: Can I use a real person's or a celebrity's face as a reference?
qna/real-person-celebrity-reference.summary: Our terms prohibit uploading or creating content that infringes the intellectual property of others and content that is harmful or inappropriate. There is no separate clause dealing only with real people's faces. We recommend using faces you have consent for, or invented characters.

qna/seedance-2-5-length-resolution.title: What length and resolution can Seedance 2.5 produce?
qna/seedance-2-5-length-resolution.summary: In the XCONDA Video Generator, choosing Seedance 2.5 lets you generate from text, images, start and end frames, or references (Ref-to-video). Per the model's developer ByteDance Seed, Seedance 2.5 produces up to 30 seconds of video with audio in one pass. Results record resolution, aspect ratio and length — for example 720P, 16:9, 20 or 27 seconds — so you can set the duration to the second. The settings bar under the prompt box controls aspect ratio (e.g. 16:9), resolution (e.g. 720p), length (e.g. 20s) and High Quality, and prompts can be up to 30,000 characters. Available values are listed in each settings menu.

qna/seedance-prompt-language.title: Do I have to write prompts in English?
qna/seedance-prompt-language.summary: With the XCONDA Prompt skill you edit prompts in a side-by-side Korean and English editor. Check the meaning in Korean, then paste the English working version into video generation. You do not need to write English yourself.

qna/seedance-prompt-retry.title: Do I have to rewrite the prompt from scratch if I dislike the result?
qna/seedance-prompt-retry.summary: No. In the XCONDA Prompt skill you tell it in conversation what to fix, the prompt in the editor is updated, and you generate again with it. Repeat until the shot reaches the standard you want.

qna/seedance-reference-limits.title: How many reference images and videos can I add?
qna/seedance-reference-limits.summary: In the Reference mode of XCONDA video generation you can add up to 30 images, 10 videos and 10 audio clips at a time. Assets you add are kept in the Input Assets library, and you type @ in the prompt to point at the asset you mean.

qna/skills-claude-paid-plan.title: Do I need a paid Claude plan to use the skills?
qna/skills-claude-paid-plan.summary: Anthropic's help centre states that skills are available on the Free, Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans, with code execution enabled in settings. Usage limits differ by plan, so a paid plan is easier if you work on long scenarios often. Claude's policy can change — check the Claude help centre for the current rules.

qna/sound-and-editing.title: How are sound and editing handled?
qna/sound-and-editing.summary: In Cubeberry's production flow, sound is created in Suno to match the mood and length of the finished video, then video and sound are combined in Premiere Pro, where cuts, levels and subtitles are checked before final output.

qna/subscription-auto-renewal.title: Does a subscription renew automatically?
qna/subscription-auto-renewal.summary: Yes. Until you cancel, a subscription is charged automatically each month on the same date to the stored payment method. Before the first payment we show the price, billing cycle, renewal terms and how to cancel, and you agree to them; after purchase we send a confirmation email with the renewal terms and cancellation steps.

qna/subscription-credit-rollover.title: Do unused subscription credits roll over to the next month?
qna/subscription-credit-rollover.summary: Yes. Unused subscription credits roll over to the next billing cycle and are valid for up to one year from the date they were granted. Expired credits lapse automatically, and credits are consumed starting with the earliest expiry date.

qna/supported-ai-models.title: Which AI models can I use?
qna/supported-ai-models.summary: Video generation supports Seedance 2.5, and Cubeberry is an Authorized Dealer for BytePlus. Image models differ by tool: in FLEXBOARD you can choose among GPT Image 2, Seedream 5.0 Pro, GPT Image 2.5 Flare and GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, and in Turn between Gemini 3.1 Flash and GPT Image 2. Supported models change with releases — check each tool's screen for the current list.

qna/terms-change-notice.title: Will you tell me in advance if prices or terms change?
qna/terms-change-notice.summary: Yes. Price changes are announced 30 days before they take effect, and amounts already paid are charged at the old price. For subscriptions, the new price applies from the first billing date after the notice period, and you can cancel before then. Changes to the terms are announced 7 days in advance (30 days for changes unfavourable to members), and material changes to the privacy policy at least 30 days in advance.

qna/turn-image-usage.title: Where do images made in Turn get used?
qna/turn-image-usage.summary: Three places. Empty-space images (Freeze Frame) become background references for Seedance video generation; key images with a character become FLEXBOARD storyboard shots; and the space image becomes the stage for blocking in Blocking Board.

qna/turn-props-wallpaper.title: Can I add props or change wallpaper in Turn?
qna/turn-props-wallpaper.summary: Yes. In Wall Edit, choose one of the six direction cards, upload a reference image, paint the area you want to change and run it. Use INPAINT for a single prop (only the painted area is edited), REGEN to regenerate a whole wall of that direction, and REPLACE to swap a specific object. For broad surfaces such as wallpaper, pair the reference image with an instruction like "remove the moulding and change only the wallpaper" for a clean result.

qna/turn-room-size-credits.title: Does changing the room size in Turn cost more credits?
qna/turn-room-size-credits.summary: No. Change the room's width, depth and ceiling height in Room Size · Camera, then press "Apply Room Size · No Additional Generation" — the proportions change using the existing wall images without generating new ones, and props stay in place.

qna/turn-without-photos.title: Can I use Turn without any photos?
qna/turn-without-photos.summary: Yes. Leave all four reference slots (Front, Left, Right, Back) empty and the space is built from your written description alone. One front photo is also enough, and you can add photos of whichever directions you have.

qna/uploaded-content-usage.title: Does Cubeberry use the images and videos I upload?
qna/uploaded-content-usage.summary: You own the images and videos you upload and the work you create. Cubeberry may use that content to provide and improve the service. It is used to train XCONDA models only with your consent. We do not sell personal data and do not share it for targeted advertising.

qna/video-generation-inputs.title: What should I put into the video generation screen?
qna/video-generation-inputs.summary: Four things together: 1) reference images (character sheet, background sheet, props) to pin faces, wardrobe and space; 2) a storyboard (per-shot images) to pin framing and shot order; 3) a Seedance prompt in English for movement, timing and camera; 4) a blocking puppet clip to pin blocking and movement paths. Whatever you leave out, the model fills in on its own.

qna/what-is-blocking-board.title: What is Blocking Board?
qna/what-is-blocking-board.summary: Blocking Board is a digital rehearsal tool that checks whether people, space and camera work together before you generate video; it will be offered on the web. You draw character positions and movement paths on a floor plan, play the scene on a 3D stage and check sight lines, the 180-degree line and collisions. It can also export a clip of puppets moving through the space, which you can feed into video generation.

qna/what-is-flexboard.title: What is FLEXBOARD?
qna/what-is-flexboard.summary: FLEXBOARD is a storyboard tool that splits a scenario into shots and previews each shot with text and an image. You check framing and characters before generating video, then fix only the shots you dislike. It is designed to be used together with Seedance 2.5.

qna/what-is-turn.title: What is Turn?
qna/what-is-turn.summary: Turn builds a virtual set you can orbit 360 degrees from a single photo or a written description. Because you create one space and rotate the camera inside it, doors, windows and props stay where they were as shots change. You can add a character at the angle you like and produce key images from it.

qna/what-is-xconda.title: What is XCONDA?
qna/what-is-xconda.summary: XCONDA is an AI video and image production platform run by Cubeberry (xconda.ai). It gives you several generative models in one place plus production tools — FLEXBOARD, Turn, Blocking Board and others — that carry a project from scenario to storyboard to generated video. The focus is not a single clip but work in which many shots hold the same characters in the same space.

qna/what-is-xconda-claude-skill.title: What is an XCONDA skill for Claude?
qna/what-is-xconda-claude-skill.summary: A skill is a task tool for XCONDA work that you add to Claude. There are two. The FLEXBOARD skill splits a scenario into shots and checks the total running time, how much action each shot carries, whether similar shots sit next to each other and jar, and how many characters are on screen. The XCONDA Prompt skill builds Seedance 2.5 prompts from the key images you locked in FLEXBOARD, written as if four directors — overall, camera, lighting and art — each had a say.

qna/where-to-get-skills.title: Where do I get the skills?
qna/where-to-get-skills.summary: The Claude skills for the XCONDA production workflow (FLEXBOARD skill and XCONDA Prompt skill) are downloaded from the XCONDA hub. Add the downloaded file to Claude using the installation steps.

qna/who-made-xconda.title: Who made XCONDA?
qna/who-made-xconda.summary: XCONDA is developed and operated by Cubeberry Co., Ltd., based in Korea. Cubeberry was founded in 2023 and designed by CEO Jinseo Lee, a former KBS drama PD, together with a broadcast writer, working directors and AI video artists. The XCONDA pipeline produced KBS 1TV's "Legend of the Haunted: Gumiho" (May 2025 — the first AI animation broadcast in prime time by a Korean broadcaster), KBS documentary "Korean War Mobile Trauma Centre" (June 2025) and the generative AI parts of KBS 1TV documentary "Sacred Object" (aired March 2026), and is producing four AI web dramas in KOCCA's New Media Technology Content Lab. Cubeberry has delivered more than 3,100 broadcast-grade AI shots.

qna/why-faces-change-between-cuts.title: Why does the face change from shot to shot in AI video?
qna/why-faces-change-between-cuts.summary: Given only text, a video model imagines each frame anew, so faces, clothing and framing drift even when you describe the same character. Anything that must stay the same has to be pinned visually: faces and wardrobe with reference images, the space with a background image, and framing with a storyboard. XCONDA's workflow is built so that pinning happens before video generation.

qna/why-puppet-video.title: Why do I need a puppet clip?
qna/why-puppet-video.summary: Movement like "enters through the left door, walks around the table and stops by the window" often goes the wrong way when written as text, and several characters moving at once is hard to control in words. Adding a puppet clip lets Seedance read the blocking from video rather than text. The puppet does not need to look human — position, direction and speed are enough.

qna/xconda-video-workflow-overview.title: What is the full workflow for making a video with XCONDA?
qna/xconda-video-workflow-overview.summary: Cubeberry's production flow has seven steps: 1) write the scenario; 2) secure reference images (character sheet, Turn backgrounds); 3) write the written board and storyboard prompts (FLEXBOARD skill); 4) build the storyboard and blocking clip (FLEXBOARD, Blocking Board); 5) write the Seedance prompts and generate video; 6) produce sound; 7) combine video and sound. Step 4, the storyboard, is where preparation hands over to generation. The hub blog post "From one scenario to a finished video" walks through it.

qna/xconda-vs-other-ai-video-tools.title: How is XCONDA different from other AI video tools?
qna/xconda-vs-other-ai-video-tools.summary: XCONDA puts more weight on the stage before generation. Give a video model text alone and faces, wardrobe and framing drift from shot to shot. XCONDA's workflow pins faces, space, framing and blocking first — with FLEXBOARD (per-shot storyboard), Turn (360° virtual set) and Blocking Board (movement paths) — and then generates video. It is broadcast drama practice transferred to AI video.
